svg.title: Bioenergetics overview
svg.desc: Photosynthesis: Carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen. Light transfers energy to chloroplasts; chlorophyll absorbs it. Endothermic: energy is taken in. Plants respire all the time; photosynthesis needs light. Use the glucose: Respiration; starch and fat/oil storage; cellulose cell walls. Glucose plus nitrate-derived nitrogen → amino acids → proteins. Limiting factors: Light, CO₂, temperature and chlorophyll can limit rate. A plateau means extra light alone will not help. Intensity ∝ 1/distance²; doubling distance quarters intensity. Greenhouses: balance extra crop income against heat/light/CO₂ costs. Pondweed practical: Change lamp distance; measure oxygen volume/time. Control temperature, CO₂ supply, plant and background light. Acclimatise; repeat; calculate mean. Bubbles vary in size, so volume is usually better. Rate = volume/time; plot against light intensity or 1/distance². Respiration pathways: Aerobic: glucose + O₂ → CO₂ + water; more energy transferred. Anaerobic: muscles → lactic acid; yeast/plants → ethanol + CO₂. Less energy per glucose. Respiration is exothermic and continuous; fermentation makes bread rise and produces alcohol. Exercise & metabolism: Exercise raises heart rate, breathing rate/volume. Oxygen shortage → more anaerobic respiration and fatigue. Oxygen debt: extra oxygen needed afterwards. Blood takes lactic acid to liver → glucose. Metabolism = all cell/body reactions; builds carbohydrates, lipids and proteins; excess nitrogen → urea.
